## Release Notes for 32.6.10

[Windows Installer](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.6.10/draw.io-32.6.10-windows-installer.exe)
[Windows No Installer (zip)](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.6.10/draw.io-32.6.10-windows.zip)
[macOS - Universal](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.6.10/draw.io-universal-32.6.10.dmg)
Linux - [deb](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.6.10/drawio-amd64-32.6.10.deb), [AppImage](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.6.10/drawio-x86_64-32.6.10.AppImage) or [rpm](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.6.10/drawio-x86_64-32.6.10.rpm)

**ChangeLog:**

- Uses electron 44.10.2
- Exports all pages as one SVG with --all-pages -f svg, with a view for each page, so that file.svg#Page-2 in an image shows the second page [jgraph/drawio#5821]
- Stops the command line export from hanging on malformed PNG files
- Updates to [draw.io core 32.6.10](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio/blob/v32.6.10/ChangeLog). All changes from 32.6.1 to 32.6.10 are added in this build.

**Testing:**

Verified against the packaged, signed macOS build. Windows and Linux packages were verified from the produced release artifacts, their sizes and update manifests, rather than by running them.

Base checks

- Launch, open a file passed on the command line, add and edit shapes, change styles, undo and redo, copy and paste, save and reopen, insert, rename and delete pages, and zoom
- Export to PNG and PDF from the app, and to PNG, JPEG, SVG, PDF, XML and HTML from the command line, covering scale, border, transparency, cropping, page selection with -p and --size page
- Diagram round trip in an exported PDF, including reopening the exported PDF and recovering both pages
- Mermaid and CSV import, and the --layout and --normalize options from the command line
- Shape search, stencils and shape libraries, and the export, print and Page Setup dialogs
- Settings and the window position and size survive a restart
- The Quick Look extension is registered for this build, sandboxed and separately signed
- The macOS bundle is signed with a Developer ID certificate under the hardened runtime, is notarised and stapled
- The Electron security fuses are applied
- 296 unit tests pass

All pages as one SVG

- A file with 2 pages exports one SVG with a view for the name and the ID of each page, and in a browser the views show the second page and no view shows the first page
- A file with 3000 pages exports in about 6 seconds with all of its views
- A page with math, a page with a traced image and the page after them all arrive in the SVG
- The Alt Text of each page is written as its title with markup escaped, and pages without one have none

Malformed PNG files

- Five crafted PNG files, each in a folder export and as a listed file with -f html, end without hanging, and the good diagram next to them is still exported. Three of them hung the previous release on both paths
- A PNG with an embedded diagram is still found by a folder export, and a PNG without one is skipped

Checks around the changes

- Edges with the outline perimeter end on the outline of an image in SVG and PDF exports, also for the PDF export of a .drawio.svg file
- Relative links in SVG exports are written without the install path, and javascript: links lose their scheme
- A .mmd file with a title and description opens with them as the Alt Text of the page, and SVG exports write them as the title
- Opening a diagram with a data source makes no request, and file URLs are refused as data sources
- Alt+Shift+D describes the selection and Alt+Shift+U opens the text outline
- Three library saves without a dialog each reach the file, and drafts are written next to the file and read back
- Reads, stats and writes of paths the user has not authorised are still refused [GHSA-fjgc-8xgj-rvh4]

detail.readme_excerpt:
About
----- 

**drawio-desktop** is a diagramming desktop app based on [Electron](https://electronjs.org/) that wraps the [core draw.io editor](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio).

Download built binaries from the [releases section](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases).

**Can I use this app for free?** Yes, under the GPL v3 license. If you don't change the code and accept it is provided "as-is", you can use it for any purpose.

Windows installation
--------------------

Three flavours of Windows download are published on the [releases page](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases):

- `draw.io-<version>-windows-installer.exe` — NSIS installer. Installs **per-machine** into `Program Files` and **requires administrator privileges**.
- `draw.io-<version>.msi` — MSI installer. Installs **per-user** into the user's profile and **does not require administrator privileges**. Use this one if you don't have admin rights on your machine.
- `draw.io-<version>-windows.zip` — portable build. Extract the zip anywhere and run `draw.io.exe`, with no installation (and therefore without admin rights). File-type associations are not registered.

The Microsoft Store (APPX) build is also installable per-user without admin rights via the Store.

### Windows on Arm

draw.io Desktop is built natively for Windows on Arm (ARM64) and is supported on Windows 11 ARM64 devices. Two native ARM64 downloads are published with every release:

- `draw.io-arm64-<version>-windows-arm64-installer.exe` — NSIS installer, per-machine, requires administrator privileges.
- `draw.io-arm64-<version>-windows-arm64-no-installer.exe` — portable build, no installation or admin rights needed.

The MSI and Microsoft Store builds are x64 only and run under emulation on ARM64 devices. ARM64 builds up to and including 31.4.4 were shipped with auto-update disabled; install a newer release manually once, after which the ARM64 installer build updates itself like x64.

Linux installation
------------------

If you manage AppImages with [AppImageLauncher](https://github.com/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher), you need a 3.0 release of it (currently labelled beta). Since 31.4.2 the AppImage uses the static AppImage runtime so that it no longer depends on the end-of-life `libfuse2`, and AppImageLauncher 2.2.0, the last stable release, cannot load a static runtime. The app then fails to start with:

```
fuse: memory allocation failed
squashfuse 0.5.2 (c) 2012 Dave Vasilevsky
...
Can't open squashfs image: Bad address
```

Install a current AppImageLauncher from its [releases page](https://github.com/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases), which provides .deb packages, or uninstall AppImageLauncher altogether. It is not needed to run the AppImage. See [#2538](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/issues/2538) for the detail.
